inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 sales ~EUR46.5bn per the FY2025 results release (2026-02-26) as summarised in SGO.PA_Analysis.json; the last filed annual in Extracted/ is FY2024 at EUR46,571m (URD FY2024). The two differ by <0.2%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares H1 2025, 499,007,648 (H1-2025 interim L643). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Ongoing buybacks (EUR400m/yr target, ~4-5m shares/yr) make the flat count conservative by ~1%/yr; buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2024: net cash from operating activities 5,569 - capex (PP&E + intangibles + change in supplier payables) 2,083 - lease principal repaid 722 = 2,764 (URD FY2024 L24252, L24254, L24282). Lease principal is deducted because this model treats leases as an operating cost (treatment B). Interest paid is classified in operating by Saint-Gobain, so this is a levered figure; the engine rebuilds an unlevered owner FCF from components and this line is the audit anchor only. Saint-Gobain's own 'free cash flow' (EUR4.0bn FY2024, EUR3.75bn FY2025) excludes additional-capacity capex and is not comparable.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net-debt company (ex-lease net debt EUR9.7bn against owner FCF ~EUR2.7-3.0bn); interest income on the gross cash pile (EUR301m FY2024) is netted inside the cost of net debt, and gross cash is netted inside net_debt, so nothing is stripped. Investment income is not in EBITDA.
inputs.sbc_source: URD FY2024 statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payments' 72 (L24347); FY2023 62. No separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0 every year). SBC is 0.15% of revenue: an effectively SBC-zero filer.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: FY2024 '(Increase) decrease in treasury stock' (811) (URD FY2024 L24269); H1 2025 (401). New EUR400m target set for 2025; Lead & Grow plan earmarks ~EUR8bn for dividends + buybacks 2026-2030.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Latest filing in Extracted/ is the H1 2025 interim: gross debt ex-leases 15,722, cash 5,990, lease liabilities 3,055, total net debt (Saint-Gobain definition, incl. leases) 12,787 (H1-2025 interim L2343-2349). The FY2025 results release reports total net debt EUR10.4bn at 2025-12-31 (secondary source: Analysis.json); the EUR2.4bn H2 2025 reduction is carried as an explicit equity_bridge line so that it can be replaced by the FY2025 URD figure once that filing is extracted, rather than being buried in the anchor.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate: 10y OAT ~3.4%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.15 (rate-sensitive construction cyclical) -> cost of equity ~9.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.7% (EUR green bonds 2024 at 3.0-3.6%), 26.5% tax -> 2.7% after tax; weights ~82% equity (market cap ~EUR33bn) / 18% ex-lease net debt (~EUR7.3bn at Dec-2025). WACC 8.3% for all three scenarios: cyclicality and integration risk are charged in the flows and the scenario weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full IFRS-16 lease cash (FY2024 principal 722 + interest 96 = 818, 1.76% of sales) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (3,055 at H1 2025) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. EBITDA margin anchor is Saint-Gobain's post-IFRS-16 EBITDA (which already deducts short-term/variable lease expense of ~EUR234m); D&A path is PP&E + intangibles only (1,410 FY2024, 3.0% of sales), ex right-of-use depreciation, so the lease is charged once. Sanity multiples must therefore compare ex-lease EV with EBITDA less lease cash (~EUR6.4bn), not with the headline EUR7.2bn.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of EBITDA); non-controlling interests charged once, in the equity bridge, at ~10x their FY2024 profit share (EUR90m, URD FY2024 L24182) = EUR900m, versus EUR513m book. Calibration: FY2024 modelled NOPAT (pre-SBC EBITDA 7,277 - SBC 72 - lease 818 - D&A 1,410 = EBIT 4,977; x 73.5% = 3,658) ties to recurring net income 3,474 + after-tax net borrowing cost ~186 = 3,660.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US cyclical industrial; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2, with owner-fcf-adaptations for EUR WACC, IFRS-16 leases, NCI and the matching-asset rule). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. SBC-ZERO: SBC is 0.15% of revenue, so house and street bases almost coincide and band_position should be read as degenerate. FY0 = FY2025 (results published 2026-02-26) so that Y1 = FY2026, the current year; FY2025 and H1 2026 figures come from the Analysis JSON because the FY2025 URD and H1 2026 interim are not yet in Extracted/ -- the orchestrator should fetch both and rerun this as an UPDATE (the reconciliation bridge will then test the +2,400 roll-forward line directly). Q3 2026 trading update is due ~2026-10-29/30, after this valuation date. Non-operating income/expense (~EUR236m/yr of restructuring etc.) is left inside EBITDA as a recurring cost. PPA amortisation (EUR233m) and impairments (EUR291m FY2024) sit below operating income and are not in the flows. Future M&A (the plan's ~EUR12bn growth capex/M&A envelope) is NOT modelled: acquisitions at fair prices are value-neutral and their revenue is not in the growth paths; the EUR4.5bn of 2024-25 deals (CSR, Bailey, Fosroc, Cemix, Ovniver) is already in the FY2025 base. US asbestos (DBMP Chapter 11, ~$407m provision, payments suspended) is treated as a bear-case risk rather than a bridge deduction. Price is a regular Friday close, not after-hours.

equity_bridge.item: H2 2025 net-debt reduction to the Dec-2025 balance sheet
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 results release: total net debt EUR10.4bn at 2025-12-31 (incl. ~EUR3.1bn leases) vs EUR12,787m at 2025-06-30 in the H1 2025 interim (filing anchor). H2 is structurally the cash-generative half (dividend paid in June; FY2025 free cash flow EUR3.75bn). SECONDARY SOURCE (Analysis.json) -- replace with the FY2025 URD net-debt note when extracted. Worth ~EUR4.8/share.

Provisions for pensions and other employee benefits 1,599 (H1-2025 interim L584) less pension plan surpluses 316 (URD FY2024 L24112) = ~1,283, x (1 - 26%) = ~950. Debt-like; service cost already sits in EBITDA.
~10x FY2024 NCI share of net income (EUR90m); book value EUR513m. Charged once, here, because the flows are consolidated.
URD FY2024 balance sheet L24110. Their income (share of associates, EUR44m) is reported below operating income and is therefore not in the EBITDA flows: matching-asset rule.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Lead & Grow 2026-2030 target of mid-single-digit local-currency growth, haircut ~1pt for persistent FX translation drag and ex-M&A; equity 5y CAGR (5.3%) and revenue 5y CAGR (1.8%) bracket it.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 5.3% diverges >30% from revenue 5y CAGR 1.8% (buyback-shrunk count, 2022 price-led revenue spike then FX/divestment reversal) and from EPS 5y CAGR 16.9% (FY2019 base year carried EUR0.6bn of Sika-settlement/impairment charges). None of the three is a clean forward proxy; growth is anchored to guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are FY2019->FY2024 (5y) and FY2021->FY2024 (3y), the last filed annuals. FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series: OCF - capex - IFRS-16 lease principal - SBC = 1,113 (FY2019), 2,623, 2,178, 3,054, 3,309, 2,692 (FY2024); lease principal 815/766/762/725/693/722 from each URD's cash-flow statement. Owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported-FCF CAGR only because the fixed lease deduction shrank relative to a growing base; both start from a 2019 trough that predates the 2021+ margin step-change and are not a projection basis. Pre-IFRS-16 years (FY2016-18) are comparable without the lease deduction because rents were then inside OCF.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +0.5% reported: H1 2026 sales -1.1% reported (+0.7% LFL, Q2 +3.5% LFL) with FX drag; H2 laps a weak H2 2025. FY2027-30 3.5-4.0%: mid-single-digit local-currency plan target less ~1pt FX/portfolio drag, no unannounced M&A. Fades to 2.0% by Y10.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin anchor 15.65% (FY2024 7,205 + 72 SBC over 46,571; FY2025 15.5% reported). FY2026 15.2% honours guidance 'above 15%' with the weather-hit H1. Then climbs to 16.5%, the lower-middle of the Lead & Grow 15-18% range, as construction chemicals (~20% EBITDA margin) and CSR/Bailey synergies mix in. D&A 3.0% -> 3.3% as capex above D&A and acquired PP&E depreciate. Capex 4.5% per guidance, easing to 4.3% as growth fades. Cash tax 26.5% (FY2024 cash tax 1,094 on pre-tax 3,994 = 27.4%, statutory France 25.8%). WC -3.5% of incremental revenue (operating WC 1,576 = 3.4% of sales, 12 days).
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.3%/2.0% implies ~16.2x terminal owner FCF; cap set at 15x for a construction cyclical, so the cap binds mildly in the base case.

scenario_narratives.base: Construction demand recovers slowly and unevenly: European renovation grinds higher from a multi-year trough, North American new-build stays soft until rates fall further, India/SE Asia/Australia (CSR) and construction chemicals (Fosroc, Cemix) outgrow the group. FY2026 is a flat, weather-dented year at the 'above 15%' EBITDA margin; from 2027 the Lead & Grow plan delivers mid-single-digit local-currency growth with ~1pt lost to FX translation, and mix (construction chemicals at ~20% margin, synergies on EUR4.5bn of 2024-25 deals) lifts the EBITDA margin to 16.5%, the lower-middle of the 15-18% target. Capex stays at the guided 4.5% of sales; no further M&A is counted. Owner FCF runs ~6-7% of sales, roughly EUR3bn today rising to ~EUR4.4bn by 2035.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate cuts unlock the pent-up US and European new-build cycle in 2027-28 while energy-renovation programmes and decarbonisation rules (low-carbon plasterboard, glass, construction chemistry) pull demand toward Saint-Gobain's differentiated systems. Local-for-local manufacturing turns the tariff regime into share gains against importers. Growth runs at the top of the plan (5-5.5% for three years), the EBITDA margin reaches 17.5% (upper half of the 15-18% range) on construction-chemicals mix and CSR/Bailey synergies, and asset rotation keeps ROCE above 13%. Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The new-build downturn deepens and spreads: US housing starts stay depressed, China new-build keeps shrinking, and the European recovery stalls, so sales fall 2% in 2026 and are flat in 2027. Pricing in commoditised insulation, plasterboard and mortars breaks under CRH/Holcim/Knauf competition and an energy-cost spike (2022-style) is only partly passed through, taking the EBITDA margin back to 14% (FY2023 was 14.6%, FY2020 ~12%). Integration of 24+ simultaneous acquisitions disappoints, management cuts capex to 4% to protect the balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA already 1.7x at H1 2025), and the DBMP asbestos ring-fence is challenged in court. Terminal growth 1.5% at a 13x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; here 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the company is a rate-sensitive construction cyclical currently in a demand trough (FY2026 guidance was cut below the FY2025 margin, H1 2026 LFL flat), carries an unusually heavy integration load (CSR, Bailey, Fosroc, Cemix, Ovniver inside 18 months, net debt/EBITDA up to 1.7x) and an unresolved US asbestos ring-fence. Bull cut to 25% because it needs a synchronised US and European new-build recovery AND margins in the upper half of the plan range AND clean integration at the same time. No going-concern or covenant risk (investment grade, EUR6-8bn gross cash), so bear is not pushed further.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero filer (SBC 0.15% of revenue): house and street bases differ by ~EUR2.4/share, so the accounting-regime band collapses and band_position is not meaningful. The engine's arithmetic value (price far below the house IV, divided by a ~EUR2.4 band) would print as a large negative number; read it as n/a.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Saint-Gobain is valued as a mature, moderately cyclical industrial compounder whose 2018-2025 portfolio rotation permanently lifted the margin and cash-conversion profile (EBITDA margin 15.5% vs ~11% pre-2018; ROCE 14% vs 10.7%). Value comes from a steady ~6-7% owner-FCF margin on ~EUR47-62bn of sales compounded at 3-4%, discounted at a EUR 8.3% WACC with the terminal multiple capped at 15x owner FCF. Leases are charged as an operating cost (principal + interest) and excluded from net debt; pensions, NCI and associates are bridged explicitly. The market price at ~6.3x EV/EBITDA (lease-inclusive) and ~10x recurring earnings sits well below the base case: the question the model poses is whether the post-2018 margin structure holds through a downturn, which is exactly what the bear case tests.
key_risks_to_valuation: Balance-sheet vintage: the EUR2.4bn H2 2025 net-debt reduction (worth ~EUR4.8/share) is a secondary-sourced roll-forward until the FY2025 URD is extracted; the FY2025 and H1 2026 flows likewise come from the Analysis JSON rather than filings.
Cyclical margin durability: every scenario assumes the EBITDA margin stays above 14%; FY2020 printed ~12% and the model has no sub-14% path.
Terminal-value weight: the 15x cap binds in base and bull, so ~55-60% of EV is terminal; a 13x cap (bear) is worth roughly EUR8/share on the base case.
FX translation: ~70% of sales are outside the eurozone; a strong EUR has cost 2-4pts of reported growth in 2024-26 and the growth paths carry only ~1pt of drag.
Unmodelled M&A: the plan's ~EUR12bn growth-capex/M&A envelope is assumed value-neutral; overpaying (or a transformational deal) is not in the paths.
US asbestos (DBMP Chapter 11 ring-fence) and EU carbon costs (ETS/CBAM on glass melting) are tail liabilities left to the bear weight rather than the bridge.
